status: successful compiler probe, not an integrated inventory gate
command: RUSTFLAGS='--force-warn unsafe_code' cargo check -p martensite-tkernel --tests --target TARGET --message-format=json
measurement: Number of compiler-message events with message.code.code equal to unsafe_code, grouped by Cargo target name. These are emitted diagnostics, NOT unique unsafe sites. Library and library-test compilations repeat production diagnostics.
exclusions: Only tkernel, its selected test targets and compiled dependencies were requested; this is not a workspace-wide inventory.
Precompiled standard-library unsafe and host build-script/procedural-macro implementations are not inventoried by these target checks.
Inactive cfg branches, unselected features, doctests and native runtime behavior are outside this probe.
Raw logs are temporary local evidence, not committed reproducible baselines; hashes identify the observed runs but do not archive them.
Cross-target cargo rustc --profile test --emit=metadata probes failed at linking and are excluded from these successful check results.
integration_requirements: Keep forced-warning inventory separate from normal deny/forbid acceptance checks: force-warn overrides lint levels.
Parse package identity, target identity, full primary spans and macro expansion chains; target names alone are not package identities.
Define compilation-unit multiplicity explicitly; never label aggregate library/test diagnostics as unique constructs.
Require a successful terminal build-finished event and successful process status; reject truncated or failed compiler streams.
Use locked dependencies and the pinned compiler for the integrated collector; retain target, features, revision and toolchain provenance.
Archive normalized reports and add regression fixtures for macro expansion, cfg differences, dependencies, malformed streams and failed builds.
Integrate through the existing xtask and single CI workflow while retaining the inactive-cfg lexical ratchet.
